subject: Business Models
title: Net Revenue Retention
description: Learn Net Revenue Retention in one minute.

hook.text: Snowflake's net revenue retention exceeded 170%. Existing customers spent 70% more year over year.

buildup.text: NRR measures whether your current subscribers are spending more or less than they did last year.

discovery.text: NRR above 100% means you grow even without new customers. Expansion revenue exceeds churn.

twist.text: NRR above 130% is so rare that investors pay premium valuations for it. It signals product-market fit.

climax.text: NRR is the subscription industry's best measure of product stickiness and customer love.

punchline.text: Grow without new customers. NRR above 100% means the product sells itself.

quiz.question: What does NRR above 100% indicate?
options: Existing customers spend more than they churn

details.summary: Net revenue retention measures how much revenue from existing subscribers grows or shrinks over time, excluding new customer revenue. NRR above 100% means existing customers spend more each period through upgrades and expansions, even after accounting for churn and downgrades.
details.whyItMatters: NRR above 100% means a subscription business grows even without acquiring a single new customer. The best SaaS companies achieve 120-140% NRR, meaning their existing customers expand spending faster than others churn.
takeaways: NRR above 100% means existing customers generate more revenue over time
Top SaaS companies achieve 120-140% net revenue retention annually
High NRR reduces dependence on new customer acquisition for growth

faq.question: How does net revenue retention compound business growth?
faq.answer: At 130% NRR, a cohort of customers generating $1M in year one will generate $1.3M in year two, $1.69M in year three, all with zero new sales. Each new cohort added compounds on top. Companies with high NRR grow exponentially faster than those relying solely on new customer acquisition.

faq.question: What drives net revenue retention above 100%?
faq.answer: Usage-based pricing where customers naturally consume more over time. Seat-based pricing where teams grow. Upselling to higher tiers with premium features. Cross-selling complementary products within the platform. The key is designing products where success naturally increases spending.
